reason: The giant may redirect distant icy bodies, addressing the first goal.
expectation: I expect the giant to send some icy bodies inward, though their eventual paths are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments may reveal what happens to leftover matter, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: The giant sent icy bodies inward, opening several possible encounters along their paths.
reaction: I am curious what happens to their ice in warmer space.
reason: Following the icy bodies into warm space directly continues their journey toward the star.
expectation: I expect some ice to evaporate or form a visible cloud, though the exact outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The bodies could encounter the rocky world, but I want to see what warmth does first.

effect: The warming ice released gas and embedded dust, showing one fate of the inward-bound bodies.
reaction: The immense thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking image.
reason: An encounter with the rocky world follows another possible path for the old ice.
expectation: Some icy bodies may strike the world and leave material on it, though their effect is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments' fate in warm space also addresses the second goal, but I want to follow the ice further first.

effect: The icy impacts cratered the world without guaranteeing an ocean, completing the ice goal.
reaction: The distinction between delivering ice and making an ocean was useful.
reason: The remaining goal concerns leftover fragments, so I will follow them into the giant's rings.
expectation: I expect the fragments to encounter and perhaps alter the rings, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Warm space is another possible destination for the fragments, but the rings seem worth exploring first.

effect: A rocky fragment struck the rings and sent icy material above their plane, revealing one fate of the leftover debris.
reaction: The spray makes the rings feel more dynamic than their smooth appearance suggests.
reason: This is the only remaining combination, and it follows the fragments into warm space.
expectation: I expect the fragments to disperse or change in warm space, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: Collisions ground some leftover stones into fine dust, which can now be combined with material released from the ice.
reaction: The fragments gaining a different role between worlds is a satisfying continuation.
reason: This is the only available combination and may show what happens when the two dust sources meet.
expectation: I expect the dust and gas to mingle in warm space, though the outcome is uncertain.

effect: The two dust sources mingle and scatter starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to connect the two paths of leftover material.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the icy bodies into warm space was most worthwhile: the small remnant trailing an immense, thin cloud was a striking image.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grinding leftover stones into dust felt fairly predictable, though it set up the final combination.

surprise.text: The icy impacts created craters but did not guarantee an ocean; that distinction changed my expectation of what ice delivery means.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary, although the final combination was the only available option rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more connections between familiar astronomical objects and the material they leave behind.
